title: My ten days and spending plan
subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Summer 1: Dealings with others and Important Lessons
source: Seeded from islamic-studies/y9 lesson 30 (Pupil PDF worksheet: my ten days and spending plan)
intro: Lesson 30: Dhul-Hijjah: the best ten days and wealth spent for Allah. To understand the virtue of the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah and how Muslims use their wealth for Allah in them through the udhiyah and sadaqah

questions.q: Explain why the udhiyah must be from halal money.
questions.a: Allah is pure and accepts only what is pure (Muslim); worship from haram wealth is not accepted; taqwa is what reaches Allah (22:37).
questions.model: Point: worship must be pure. Evidence: 'Allah is pure and accepts only what is pure' (Muslim). Explain: an udhiyah bought with haram money defeats its purpose. Link: 22:37.

questions.q: Fasting the Day of Arafah expiates ...
questions.a: The year before and the year after
options: The year before and the year after

questions.q: Plan in the portal response box: 'My ten days': a deed for each day and a £100 (imagined) spending plan for Allah, with reasons and evidence for two choices. Start: 'Day 1: ...'
questions.a: Ten deeds; a spending plan such as a share in an udhiyah for the poor and sadaqah, with evidence
questions.model: Teacher writes: 'Day 9: fast the Day of Arafah if able (Muslim). £60: a share of an udhiyah for families in need.'

questions.q: why do some families send their udhiyah abroad, and what do scholars say about eating from it?
questions.a: To feed the poor where need is greatest; eating from it is recommended where possible, so some also sacrifice locally
